messages:
anya: Quick follow-up on the GQA/MQA kernel selection RFC — saw a perf dip in grouped-query when batch_size >= 64 and kv_window ~ 8k. Traces point to extra memcpy in the grouped path. 
kevin: Can you paste the trace snippet or perf flame?
anya: sure, pasted below
```
# cpu-hotspots
grouped_query_path::prepare_kv  42%  memcpy
grouped_query_path::route_cost  12%  serialize
kv_cache::shard_merge         18%  locks
```
matt: hmm. that memcpy is the grouped path concatenating per-query prefixes before dispatch, right?
anya: yeah — we do per-query prefix copy -> single dispatch buffer. Works for small batches but when queries have long prefixes and batching is large it dominates.
selene: is this specific to the MQA planner or the downstream kernel input format?
kevin: looks like planner arranges grouped payloads; kernel expects a packed buffer so the runtime does the pack. possible refactor: let kernel accept scatter-gather iovecs to avoid copying.
matt: iovec support would be ideal but touches kernel interface boundary. We should weigh scope: (A) add small iovec shim in runtime (B) extend kernel API to accept iovec (C) add per-slot KV pre-merge cache.
anya: quick cost estimates I ran: option A reduces memcpy time by ~60% for current workload and is lowest-risk. Option B removes copy entirely but needs kernel changes + quantized kernel validation. Option C helps warm-cache cases but doesn't address first-touch.
selene: also consider fallback policy: if selector predicts >X memcpy cost, route those queries to single-query kernels to avoid grouped overhead. That keeps runtime API stable.
matt: good point. So two parallel tracks: immediate low-risk shim + selector cost-model change; medium-term kernel API extension.
kevin: for selector: we need a compact cost signal: expected_total_copy_bytes and expected_sgd (something like tokens_saved). We can add a small JSON hint in selector output: {"copy_bytes": 12345, "tokens_saved": 27}. Runtime can use thresholds.
anya: I'll prototype the cost estimator today and add microbench harness. Can someone add a kernel-entrypoint RFC issue so we can park API discussion?
matt: I've created issue #2483 and added a short checklist. link: https://rwd.ai/infra/issue/2483 :eyes:
selene: I'll own the selector thresholds experiments. Plan: run across 3 production traces (webchat, search, docs-index) and measure P99 latency and avg token cost delta.
kevin: also add a guard in the grouped path: if total_prefix_bytes > 1MB then fallback to S-Query kernel. cheap check.
anya: done locally; falls back and avoids memcpy for heavy prefixes. pushed small PR to my fork: https://git.rwd/p/anya/mqa-memcpy-fallback (WIP).
runtime-bot: deploy-preview created by anya for branch mqa-memcpy-fallback — preview env r-qe-42 — logs: https://ci.rwd/deploy/987
matt: next sync: collect benchmark numbers in this thread and update issue 2483. can we have results by EOD Friday?
selene: yes, will run nightly jobs. :thumbsup:
anya: thanks all — will post microbench numbers here when ready.
